title: Streamline onboarding workflow and deterministic version-locking for third-party models
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: When we ingest third-party models (open checkpoint bundles or vendor-supplied artifacts) the current onboarding pipeline produces ambiguous metadata for variants (multiple quantized artifacts, different tokenizer bundles, variant-specific config overrides). This ambiguity causes incorrect default pinning, degraded runtime selection, and repeated manual fixes by oncall and onboarding engineers. Additionally, performance profiles are inconsistently published: some models have detailed latency/throughput/memory artifacts while others have only high-level notes. We need a single, deterministic manifest format and an automated publish workflow that: 1) generates an immutable pin identifier for each model variant, 2) attaches a signed performance signature artifact, and 3) updates the catalog docs and public model page atomically.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Model manifest schema v2 accepted by catalog ingestion service; 2) Each ingested variant has a stable pin id (normalized-hash + variant-tag) and is immutable once published; 3) Performance profile (latency P50/P95, throughput @common batch sizes, GPU/CPU memory footprint, and quality eval snapshot) is produced and stored alongside the manifest; 4) Publish pipeline creates a docs PR (internal Confluence or Drive link) and a catalog publish event; 5) Rollout supports canary -> org -> public gates and automatic fallback mapping to compatible pinned variants.
implementation_tasks: Spec: define manifest-v2 fields (provenance, source_uri, artifact_hash, variant_tag, quant_info, tokenizer_revision, architecture_sig, compat_matrix)
Pin service: implement deterministic pin id generator (normalized manifest -> SHA256 -> short-hex + variant tag)
Perf pipeline: add perf-signature artifact generation (bench harness + standardized metrics JSON + artifact storage link)
Ingestion: validate and reject ambiguous bundles with clear error messages and remediation guidance
Catalog UI: render variant-level pins and link to perf artifacts (console change)
Publish workflow: connect manifest publish to docs PR and runbook generation
Rollout: implement canary publish controls and automatic fallback rules for runtime routing
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Strong validation will increase initial onboarding friction for model contributors; mitigation: provide a small 'acceptance' mode allowing manual override for trusted vendors.
- Deterministic pinning requires canonicalization of manifests; we must lock ordering and field normalization to avoid repeated re-pinning.
- Attaching perf artifacts increases storage and pipeline time; tradeoff: better operational reliability and faster incident triage.
comments: 2025-10-29 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after a support incident where two quant variants were published under the same catalog id and caused production mismatches. Attached initial spec link.

2025-10-31 - Marco Liu: Implemented prototype pin-generator and validated against 12 community models. Found conflicts where tokenizer bundles differ only by metadata timestamp; added normalization rule to strip 'created_at' fields.

2025-11-03 - PM review (Lina Gomez): Suggested adding an explicit 'compat_matrix' field to manifest-v2 so runtime can decide safe fallbacks. Also requested that perf artifacts include a small sample of eval outputs for regression debugging.

2025-11-05 - Security (Jamal Turner): Quick review: storage of perf artifacts must adhere to data retention controls and not leak PII from evaluation datasets. Marked follow-up to redact eval prompts with customer data.
2025-11-07 - Marco Liu: WIP - moved ingestion validation into a new lambda, created branch 'catalog/manifest-v2' and opened draft PR. Next: wire the perf harness and update console rendering mockups.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests: manifest normalization and pin id reproducibility tests; 2) Integration: ingest 20 community models and verify pin id stability across repeated ingests; 3) E2E: publish canary to internal org, run inference bootstrapping tests, verify fallback mapping and perf links; 4) Load test: ensure catalog publish pipeline can handle 50 concurrent publishes without timing out.
migration_plan:
- Existing pinned models remain untouched; add a compatibility shim that maps old catalog ids to new variant pins where possible.
- For ambiguous legacy entries, create a migration review queue and a small UI that allows owners to select the correct variant mapping.
- Add cron job to detect duplicate artifact_hashes and alert owners.
rollout_steps: 1) Merge manifest-v2 schema and pin service to staging. 2) Run ingest job against staging corpus and validate pins. 3) Publish perf artifacts for a subset of models (10) and validate console UI. 4) Canary publish to internal orgs for 48h, collect errors and latency regressions. 5) Gradual public release with monitoring and rollback playbook.
owner_notes: Priority: align with Dedicated rollout in Nov (reserved capacity customers depend on deterministic pins for predictable cold-starts). If we hit storage concerns for perf artifacts, consider tiered retention (90d hot, archive to cold storage).
